about.title: Lodi Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Lodi's traffic pattern tells a story: San Joaquin County records show crashes cluster on Fridays between 2 and 4 p.m., often along Cherokee Lane, SR-99, Kettleman Lane, and Lower Sacramento Road. In a recent final reporting year, the city logged 128 injury collisions and 178 injured people. Behind those numbers are real people dealing with medical bills, missed work, and confusing calls from insurance adjusters. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we connect you, free of charge, with an independent personal injury attorney who can review what happened and explain your options under California law. Every case is different, and outcomes are never guaranteed, but getting informed early, before evidence disappears or memories fade, matters. If you were hurt in a Lodi collision, a short conversation with a connected attorney can help you understand what comes next without any upfront cost or obligation.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before Speaking With an Insurer

items.title: California's Clock Is Running
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash to file a personal injury claim in California, but that window can shrink to as little as six months if a government entity, like a public road authority, may be involved. An attorney can help identify which deadline applies to your situation.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce, Not Eliminate, Recovery
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover damages even if you were partly at fault, though your share of responsibility can reduce the amount. Understanding how fault gets allocated matters before you say anything to an adjuster.

items.title: Recorded Statements Can Work Against You
items.desc: The other driver's insurer may ask for a recorded statement soon after the crash, often before you know the full extent of your injuries. An attorney can advise you on what to share and help preserve evidence like scene photos, witness contacts, and crash reports.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a car accident in Lodi?
items.answer: In most cases, California law gives you two years from the date of the crash to file a personal injury lawsuit. If a government entity, such as the City of Lodi or Caltrans, may share responsibility for road conditions, that deadline can be far shorter, sometimes just six months. Speaking with an attorney early helps make sure you don't miss a critical filing window.

items.question: Does it matter that Lodi crashes tend to happen on Fridays between 2 and 4 p.m.?
items.answer: That pattern can be useful when an attorney is piecing together how a crash happened, especially near higher-volume corridors like Cherokee Lane or Kettleman Lane. It doesn't change your legal rights, but timing and location details can support your case when documented early.

items.question: Should I give a statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: You're generally not required to give a recorded statement to the other party's insurer, and doing so before you understand your injuries or the full picture can hurt your claim. An independent attorney can talk to the insurer on your behalf and help protect what you say.
